newsitem.title: PERU: Peruvian guerrillas release sick police chief.
newsitem.headline: Peruvian guerrillas release sick police chief.

text.p: Marxist guerrillas holding VIP hostages for 40th days inside the Japanese ambassador's home released a sick police chief captive early on Sunday.

The Red Cross identified the hostage as National Police General Jose Rivas Rodriguez. He was wheeled out of the residence on a gurney at 12.55 a.m. (0555 GMT) accompanied by Red Cross officials and Bishop Juan Luis Cipriani.
Rodriguez, lying face up with his bare feet sticking out from under a blanket, was taken to an ambulance and driven away to a nearby police hospital.
International Committee of the Red Cross representative Michel Mining told reporters the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels had agreed to free Rodriguez on medical grounds.
Rodriguez was the first hostage to be freed since Jan. 17 and reduced the number of captives still being held to 72.

Late on Saturday, shouts were heard from within the residence calling for officials from the Red Cross to enter, witnesses said. Red Cross officials entered the building with medical equipment, while the ambulance pulled up nearby.

The rebels originally took more than 500 hostages on Dec. 17 during a cocktail party at the diplomatic residence but have freed most of them. The remaining captives in the mined and booby-trapped compound include top Peruvian officials and Japanese diplomats and businessmen.
Red Cross officials have repeatedly said that the remaining hostages' health was stable despite claims from individual family members and colleagues that some were sick.
